newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: More work stoppages in year to Oct 1996 - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: More work stoppages in year to Oct 1996 - SNZ.

text.p: Nine work stoppages ended in October 1996 and a total of 78 stoppages ended in the year to October 31, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday.
The figures compare to seven stoppages in September, and 76 in the year to September.
In the year to October 1995 there were 63 work stoppages.

Of the nine stoppages in the October 1996 month, eight were complete strikes and one was a partial strike. Together they involved 2,501 employees and resulted in the loss of 1,989 days of work and about $248,000 in wages and salaries.
Stoppages that ended in the October year resulted in the loss of 68,964 days of work, 30 percent more than the 52,928 in the October 1995 year.

An estimated NZ$9.9 million in wages and salaries was lost in the year to October, 50 percent more than the $6.6 million in the year to October 1995, and 98 percent more than the $5.0 million in the year to October 1994.
Of the 78 stoppages ending in the October 1996 year, 42 were in the public sector and 36 were in the private sector.

Disputes regarding the negotiation of the content of employment contracts continue to be the most common cause of work stoppages, SNZ said. Sixty-three of the 78 stoppages in the year to October were of this nature.
